- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model often overpredicts recovery; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated upward momentum; cap forecast growth at 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.5) and price is near recent mean, model often drifts toward extreme lows or highs; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior 10-day average ± 1.5σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period price surges (especially after sentiment shifts to positive); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.27–0.30) and model forecasts are high, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
